question: Does the hook installed on any repository give honest, advisory-only results, and never block a push?
subjects: The audit's three shallow clones (kennethreitz/records, expressjs/serve-static, unrolled/secure), each with the same planted commit c2 on c1, copied fresh from the audit's scratch clones.
instrument_proof: Every replay and hook push records snapshots[].bytes_read and quick_tier files/bytes_read. The head snapshot's bytes equal `git ls-files | xargs cat | wc -c` at head (records 43,577; serve-static 61,525; secure 103,023), and the quick tier reads exactly the changed source files.
host: Joern is not on the host, so host runs cannot run the engine; that is the case a first-time pip user hits, and the output must say so. The Docker engine run uses the 2026-09-14 openultrasast:dev image with the worktree src mounted read-only, as the audit did; the image was not rebuilt (1.1 GB disk free, below the 4 GB threshold).

verdict.never_blocks: PASS in this sample: 10 hook pushes across the three repositories all exited 0, including `ousast` absent from PATH (rejected before) and OUSAST_PUSH_DEADLINE=abc (exit 2 before). Blocking stays an explicit opt-in (unit-tested, not exercised here).
verdict.never_hides: PASS in this sample: every incomplete run printed one plain `Skipped:` line per reason (2-5 per run), with no hex path or sha256 token. Go is named as not covered (`language not covered: go (1 changed file(s), 10 in the repository)`, and `notice: language not covered: go (10 files)` in `scan --mode quick`). The first push of a new branch says there is no base and what it checked instead.
verdict.quick_tier_within_deadline: On the host, every replay and hook push finished in 0.69-1.21 s against the 30 s deadline. The quick tier read exactly the changed source file (records 1 file / 17,449 B; serve-static 1 / 87 B; secure 1 / 193 B).
verdict.planted_js_eval: SURFACES. Quick tier: js-eval (CWE-95) and js-xss-response (CWE-79) at debug.js:2 on the host, 0.9 s, in replay and in the hook push. Engine (Docker, deadline 300): injection and output_encoding at debug.js:2, now novelty `new` / `file_added_in_head` (before: `unknown` / `base_incomplete`). The only veto is `capability_unavailable`, so it is shown as an advisory engine finding, not an alert.
verdict.planted_python_sql: STILL MISSED. No quick rule matches the %-formatted db.query string in records.py, and the host has no Joern, so nothing in the pre-push path reports it. Recorded as a coverage gap, with no rule edit.
verdict.planted_go_command: NOT DETECTED, NOW NAMED: Go has no engine frontend and no quick rules.
verdict.engine_deadline: Not solved. The Docker engine took 190.9 s wall time (head 107.6 s, base 80.7 s) against a 300 s deadline. The audit measured 261.7 s on a different image/src combination. A 30 s hook deadline still cannot hold it. --engine background starts it after the push, and the next push showed the earlier result. On the host that result says 'the engine did not run (Joern unavailable)', which is honest.

coverage_gaps: records: the planted Python SQL injection (`db.query("... '%s'" % name)`) is matched by no quick rule, before or after. Recorded as a quick-rule coverage gap; no rule was edited for a planted sample (that would be hand-tuning). On the host the engine cannot run, so nothing in the pre-push path reports it.
secure: Go has no engine frontend and no quick rules. It is now named in the terminal (language not covered: go), not detected.
The engine still cannot finish inside the 30 s hook deadline (the audit measured 260 s on 26 files); --engine background moves it after the push, graph reuse remains the later speed task.

notes: The Docker engine run used the worktree src at 591818d mounted over the stale 2026-09-14 openultrasast:dev image (not rebuilt: 1.1 GB disk free, below the 4 GB threshold). `eligibility_provenance_mismatch` still appears; the audit already suspected src/image skew, and it is not investigated here.
The run shows host paths after `Details:` because ops/ousast-docker mounts the artifact directory at its own path. Before, it showed the container path /out/...

The hook's 'not on PATH' hint first said 'pip install openultrasast', which is not on PyPI. The first proof run caught it. It was corrected to the git URL, and the replay and hook proofs were rerun on the rebuilt wheel recorded under build. The Docker engine run predates the hint fix and does not involve the hook script.
Host runs read their input. Each head snapshot's bytes equal `git ls-files | xargs cat | wc -c` at head, and the quick tier lists the files it read.
